module.label: Replay studio
module.description: Captures moments and temporarily presents clips.

steps.label: Read the same live game data
Remember kill / death anchor
steps.detail: Kills up to 30 seconds apart share the first-kill anchor. Highlights retain 30 seconds before that first kill, or before a death when no kill anchor applies.

effects.protection: The replay tracker observes its own game-data snapshots; a later save uses the anchor.

flows.label: Save a replay
flows.detail: Voice captures preserve their original trigger cutoff. Mark is a new independent review save, never a start point for a later save. Controls are published after startup and withdrawn by their runtime generation. Press | and say name Dragon steal (or save name Dragon steal) to save with a free-form local title/tag and the same Twitch title subject. Duration/full options belong before name; label text is bounded to 160 characters and never parsed as a command, number or fuzzy tag. Empty names do not save. Save-and-replay and mark accept names too, retaining their original purpose and button cutoff. Only highlights request Twitch; its existing title formatter, single-request admission and failure isolation remain authoritative. The capture library writes an explicit title atomically and preserves all other personal fields; missing titles retain prior edits. Voice uses leading actions with shared duration/full/name options; invalid options fail closed. Replay now captures 15 seconds by default without Twitch. Save-and-replay forwards duration/full even without a title. The same | gesture listens during playback; pause/resume use coordinator manual claims and stop revokes the pending continuation. Accurate cuts and editor exports honor HUB_REPLAY_VIDEO_ENCODER: nvenc tries CUDA decoding and GPU H.264 P5/CQ24; unsupported CUDA decoding retries CPU decoding with NVENC; software retains x264 veryfast/CRF18. GPU encoder capability failures retry software only after the shared conversion owner has closed the failed process, within the same total deadline and two-unit CPU budget. Cancellation, disk and invalid-media errors do not retry. Full resolution, every audio track, timing, source retention and atomic partial-file publication remain; stream-copy cuts bypass encoding. Every admitted capture emits a scoped recording.replay request containing a unique marker ID, original button time, label and duration; successful saves emit the same ID with the finished clip path. League recording queues these events on its existing poll, preserving markers across delayed encoding and file moves. No feature peer import or recording worker is added.

steps.label: Choose capture purpose and duration
steps.detail: Replay only: 3–120 seconds, default 15. Spoken mark via |: last 60 seconds by default, explicit 3–120 or full buffer. Highlight: explicit duration → kill → death → buffer, with 30-second pre-roll for kills and deaths. OBS stores 75 seconds for a useful minute plus voice/save headroom.

steps.label: Request Twitch for serious saves
steps.detail: Only highlight saves request a titled 60-second Twitch clip, passing the optional spoken save tag. Review-later and replay-only captures remain local. One worker and 90-second window coordinate with moderator !clip; chat reuses the existing clip. Twitch failures or short published clips never block the local save.

steps.label: Copy replay / encode serious cut
steps.detail: All audio tracks and originals are retained. Review-later and replay-only cuts use stream copy; a preceding keyframe can add lead-in.

steps.label: Persist purpose and capture result
steps.detail: Both original and cut retain capture purpose. Marked clips enter the pending review queue and never the automatic replay registry. Replay-only files are excluded from future footage review.

effects.intent: Save a local moment and its capture result
effects.protection: The capture owner admits one save. Only serious highlights request Twitch. Marked files are excluded from automatic replay but remain available for later review.

effects.intent: Copy or encode the admitted capture
effects.protection: Finite conversions share a bounded CPU budget.

flows.label: Play a replay
flows.detail: Explicit replay always selects Quick Replay. Short Move/Wipe/Fade handles entry and owned return; showcase retains its selected full transition. Browser handoff cues keep live/camera visible between clips. Offline and runtime management share the same inventory and linked-copy visibility. The existing source worker consumes a revision/session-scoped upcoming queue. Random playback publishes six actual next choices and refills until stopped. Drag/drop and buttons edit only upcoming entries; current clips and stale sessions cannot be changed. Final cleanup closes queue admission before releasing the source. Literal play name searches bypass tag/game matching; highlight shortcuts match complete selections. Press | and say next/pause/resume/stop during playback.

steps.label: Acquire physical playback gate
steps.detail: All automatic latest/tag/highlight/shuffle/game selections apply library eligibility: review-later and set-aside clips are excluded. Explicitly selected paths and saved compilations remain deliberate choices. Inventory requests share a fresh directory snapshot and linked originals are hidden while their cut exists. Trashed clips are excluded from both automatic and deliberate playback. Saved sequences retain their full order; new live additions are limited to 200.

steps.label: Prepare decoder while game stays live
steps.detail: Every clip decodes while hidden; handoff holds the next clip before it becomes audible or visible.

steps.label: Apply clip levels / first-frame hold
steps.detail: Pause and seek, then confirm a stable first-frame cursor before showing it through entry or revealing the next clip. Resume only after the reveal acknowledgement.

steps.label: Return only if still owner
steps.detail: Hold scoped pauses through the return transition. A newer manual scene choice prevents scene restoration and automatic resume.

steps.label: Release claim after final cleanup
steps.detail: Park the physical source and restore captured audio before releasing the playback gate.

effects.protection: The reservation begins before loading. Owned cleanup restores the previous scene only while the lease is current.
effects.watch: A second temporary presentation cannot reserve an already-owned scene. A manual choice revokes the lease.

normal.text: Can reserve an available scene before decoder preparation.

result.text: A result hold is not itself a scene lease. Replay admission and the existing temporary owner still decide whether playback can begin.

temporary.text: A second temporary reservation is refused while a lease already exists.

manual.text: A manual choice revokes an earlier replay lease. A new replay request is a new intent and may reserve again.

effects.intent: Pause configured modules until replay cleanup
effects.protection: Scoped pause claims stay held through final source cleanup. Finishing releases only this request.

effects.intent: Play clips through one owned source worker
effects.protection: Replacement cancels the old request, then waits for its final cleanup before source reuse.

flows.label: Game ends
flows.detail: The replay tracker reads image-clock running/generation state through the shared game policy, so the ending image start closes the game even while its HTTP API remains reachable. Temporary socket failures do not close a published running match or replay old kill anchors. New generations clear event IDs and anchors. Standalone tracking uses the shared GameStart/GameEnd interpreter. The existing thirty-second archive delay and previous-game clip retention are preserved.

steps.label: Keep the last game clip list
Archive highlight candidates
steps.detail: Replay-only, review-later and set-aside files are excluded. Archived paths retain aliases for the previous-game list.

effects.protection: Archive waits 30 seconds. Review-later, replay-only and set-aside files stay excluded; saved files retain their identities.

normal.text: Archiving is independent of lobby scene ownership. It does not request the screen.

result.text: Archiving is independent of lobby scene ownership. It does not request the screen.

temporary.text: Archiving is independent of lobby scene ownership. It does not request the screen.

manual.text: Archiving is independent of lobby scene ownership. It does not request the screen.

flows.label: Review saved clips

trigger.label: Review, keep or trim a clip

flows.detail: A thumbnail library and montage gallery allocate one private editor only when selected. Unsaved notes and montage drafts guard editor close/navigation. All clips, To review, Kept, Favorites and Trash are visible filters. The private editor places a large preview beside visible Start/End controls, exact-second inputs, cut audition and Save trimmed copy. Actions have 44-pixel targets and independent sliders have 36-pixel handles; narrow windows stack the editor while keeping Done reachable. Capture settings and the voice reference follow the library. Purposes remain a separate filter. Delete moves clips to recoverable library Trash and preserves original media, personal metadata and montage membership. The API snapshots settings, serializes the current-entry check with library writes, and removes deleted upcoming entries from the same playback queue. Restore reverses the Trash flag. Private previews never start OBS playback. The feature publishes a read-only voice reference through its public API; the management page renders literal text once and ignores reads after disposal. Accurate cuts and editor exports honor HUB_REPLAY_VIDEO_ENCODER: nvenc tries CUDA decoding and GPU H.264 P5/CQ24; unsupported CUDA decoding retries CPU decoding with NVENC; software retains x264 veryfast/CRF18. GPU encoder capability failures retry software only after the shared conversion owner has closed the failed process, within the same total deadline and two-unit CPU budget. Cancellation, disk and invalid-media errors do not retry. Full resolution, every audio track, timing, source retention and atomic partial-file publication remain; stream-copy cuts bypass encoding.

steps.label: Browse thumbnails and save types
steps.detail: Only visible cards request cached stills. One selected clip owns its preview and releases playback/polling when closed. Capture availability reads the existing coordinator buffer snapshot; the page offers the public Hub Start replay buffer action when stopped.

steps.label: Prepare local still / preview
steps.detail: Stills and video share the existing single preview worker, three admitted jobs and shared conversion budget; originals are never changed.

steps.label: Check library revision
steps.detail: Validate every selected path and decision before one atomic mutation; conflicts preserve the pending draft.

steps.label: Keep, set aside or change purpose
steps.detail: Set aside preserves the file and can be restored. Keep preserves purpose. Replay-ready promotion is explicit; labels and unknown fields survive.

steps.label: Save a trimmed copy
steps.detail: Optional trim preserves full resolution, every audio track, source purpose and personal metadata. Original retained.

steps.label: Publish the complete catalogue
steps.detail: The UI advances its own revision, keeps unsaved notes stable and offers the saved copy when ready.

effects.intent: Record a reversible review decision or save a shorter copy
effects.protection: The atomic library revision protects edits; no review decision deletes or overwrites media.

effects.intent: Prepare visible stills and the selected preview
effects.protection: Existing preview worker admits at most three jobs across stills and video and shares the conversion budget.
